```{r setup, include=FALSE}

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(tidyverse)
library(scales)


```




```{r}

# Read in the dataset:

listings  <- read_csv("listings_edinburgh.csv")

# Look at your dataset (run the below code straight into the console): 


glimpse(listings)


# Change room_type from character to factor

listings <- mutate(listings,
                   room_type = factor(room_type),
                               property_type = factor(property_type))
      
# Check levels:

levels(listings$room_type)

# Check frequencies:

table(listings$room_type)

# Create a better looking table (this uses the scales package loaded above; you might have to install this first):

listings |>
  count(room_type) |>  
  mutate(
    Percent = percent(n / sum(n), accuracy = 0.1)
  ) |>
  arrange(Percent)


# You can try creating a new smaller dataset; note how the mutate and select operations are chained via a pipe operator (|>):

listings_2 <- mutate(listings,
                   room_type = factor(room_type),
                   property_type = factor(property_type))

listings_2 <- listings |> mutate(room_type = factor(room_type),
                   property_type = factor(property_type)) |>
  select(room_type, property_type) 

# The above was only an exercise to show you how to create a subset, so we can delete the new smaller dataset now:

remove(listings_2)

```
